patch.value: Keep GitHub reference tags separate from import identity
Preserve curated local fields, allow shared reference tags, and retain migration-free matching of existing importer provenance.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Read issue 230 and all comments. Branch starts from main; PR229 changes workflows and docs separately. Plan: distinguish explicit importer identity from references, preserve curated linked content, retain legacy persisted provenance, and prove behavior with real SDK trackers and behavioral reverts. Task-specific gate budget applies: focused importer/sync/dependent tests, lint and typecheck; full suite only within 45 minutes.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Implemented separate durable import identity lookup; shared gh references no longer select owners or collide. Curated links merge provenance/lifecycle while deterministic importer records mirror content. New real SDK regressions pass 9/9, including no-git curated links and byte-identical legacy resync beside shared references. Reviewing existing tests that assumed tag-only ownership; updating mirror fixtures to explicit importer identities.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Behavioral revert proof in a disposable package copy: rebuilt after restoring released matchImportedIssue, prepareGithubImport and verifyImportIdempotency plus tag-only identity lookup. node --test --test-concurrency=2 test/reference-import-identity.test.ts: 14 tests, 13 fail, 1 pass. All four required scenarios fail: single curated Chore, shared references, mirror title refresh beside a reference, and byte-identical legacy resync beside a reference. The passing legacy link-marker case is existing supported behavior. Package worktree was never reverted. Fixed regressions are being rerun through pm test; full npm test follows within the task budget.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Linked pm test run passed 16/16 (real SDK trackers, both import modes, no-git linking, legacy compatibility, safe PR conflict rendering and dependency routing). Lint and typecheck pass; docstring gate documents 29 files/280 declarations; duplication gate has zero clones at the unchanged 50-token threshold across 30 authored modules. Added seeded preview/apply equivalence coverage. Full npm test is running with two workers and a 45-minute cap; npm/bun release:check and coverage are delegated to CI under the explicit task gate budget.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Optional full npm test was stopped under the task gate budget: an unrelated closeout workflow file had already used over 11 minutes before its large decision matrix. Running all 46 required importer/sync/direct-dependent and sync-workflow test files separately now, with two file workers and a hard 1200-second limit per file. CI owns full-suite and release certification.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Round 2 resumes from ed050d3 with a clean worktree. Read all four unresolved threads and the complete latest CodeRabbit review body, including its outside-diff upstream-target finding and scope-check note. Plan: synchronize all non-content side data for curated links; reject contradictory explicit identities before writes with normalized compatibility; persist/replay atomic import plans through retries; and guard outbound status/export targets. Keep review threads open for the orchestrator. Existing Projects follow-up audit records remain append-only as required by the task rules.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Round 2 side-data inventory: after a content merge, the mirror path applies native lifecycle transitions, synchronizes GitHub comments as annotations, persists github_* source dates/state/closure provenance, reports counts, links dependencies, and runs provenance/privacy gates. Curated updates now perform the same non-content steps. Body-only fetched comments route to annotations for curated items. SDK transaction contract uses payload-bound ordered steps: recovery replays the recorded original entries, mutations, targets, comments and dependency inputs before polling new GitHub data; a later normal sync observes changed input. Identity validation shares one normalized explicit-identity path across import, refresh, sync and export; contradictory values refuse before writes. Outbound sync/export now ignore shared references by default and offer explicit historical tag-only opt-in with competing-owner refusal.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Review regression baseline: 21 real-SDK cases passed across curated side data, explicit-identity refusal and spelling compatibility, six original-plan crash boundaries, upstream plan conflicts and actual sync/export HTTP writes. Added a further dependency replay case for an unchanged item in a mixed batch: record the complete original dependency input, interrupt, change the remote body, then recover the original edge. Replacing the prior fake incomplete-compensation test with a real SDK transaction also checks that compensation recovery reuses the saved plan. Broad gates cover 49 affected/import/refresh/identity/sync files, two workers, each invocation capped at 20 minutes; import-gate is partitioned by exhaustive disjoint test-name prefixes.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Final review regression run through pm test --run --progress passed 29/29 cases, including generated preview/apply agreement. Import-gate completed 73/73 cases across four alphabetic name partitions; all 56 declaration prefixes were checked for coverage by those partitions. A redundant non-letter pattern matched the Node file wrapper, was stopped, removed from linked tests and excluded from counts. The closeout workflow matrix reached its 20-minute cap after 143 passing cases with no assertion failures. Real compensation testing follows the public SDK contract: delete compensation retains history and reserves the original ID. Recovery now keeps the plan and returns github_import_plan_drift instead of applying changed input; explicit SDK restore of the original birth version then permits the exact saved plan to finish. The atomic file passed 11/11 including this refusal-and-restore case. Read-only identity exploration still exposes contradictory stored claims, while write planners refuse them.

value.author: codex-github230-1111
value.text: Behavioral revert proof, executed only in a disposable package copy with real temp SDK trackers: restoring round-one prepareGithubImport/runImport causes 4 of 6 curated side-data cases to fail (2 atomic annotation compatibility controls pass); restoring importIdentityKeys/matchImportedIssue causes all 7 explicit identity refusal/normalization cases to fail; restoring runImport and disabling persisted-plan dispatch in importGithubAtomic causes all 12 crash/dependency/missing-plan cases to fail; restoring planSync/buildExportPlan causes all 3 upstream planning, wire-write and generated preview/apply cases to fail. The same atomic replay revert makes the real incomplete-compensation/explicit-restore test fail (1/1). Every mutation was restored in a finally block; the fixed package copy is running the full review regression file again. Review thread mapping: PRRT_kwDOTbN4pM62J6R5 and PRRT_kwDOTbN4pM62KLhP use curated side-data tests; PRRT_kwDOTbN4pM62KLhK uses explicit identity cases; PRRT_kwDOTbN4pM62KLhO uses original-plan replay plus compensation. Latest CodeRabbit outside-diff upstream comment uses the three upstream cases. No review thread was replied to, resolved or reacted to.

The main item stays in_progress; releasing only this agent claim before commit and push.
